```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

**This model is a record of the publication and is not usable for
prediction.** The rate constants printed in the paper's Table 3 cannot
reproduce the paper's own fitted curve (Figure 1c) for any value of the
unreported blood volume. The sections "Why the printed rate constants cannot
reproduce Figure 1c" and "Assumptions and deviations" below give the
details.

- Citation: Liu T, Choi H, Zhou R, Chen I-W. Quantitative evaluation of the
  reticuloendothelial system function with dynamic MRI. *PLoS One*
  2014;9(8):e103576.
- Article: <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0103576>
- Correction: *PLoS One* 2015;10(3):e0122323 (PMC4370671). It changes only the
  Funding section; no model value is affected.

Liu et al. imaged the blood (vena cava) and the liver of nude mice every 3.2 s
with T2*-weighted MRI at 9.4 T during and after an IV bolus of a 25 nm
lipid-coated superparamagnetic iron oxide (SPIO) nanoparticle. They converted
the signal change to concentration through the particle's r2* relaxivity, and
fitted each animal with a two-compartment model in MATLAB SimBiology.
Compartment 1 is blood (volume `Vp`), compartment 2 is the liver Kupffer-cell
space (volume `VL`, fixed at 1e-3 L/kg). `Kin` and `Kout` are the
blood-to-liver association and liver-to-blood dissociation rate constants, and
`Ke` is extrahepatic elimination from blood. All rates are in 1/s.

```{r model}
mod <- readModelDb("Liu_2014_ironOxideNanoparticle_mouse")
mod
```

# Population

Young adult male 01b74 athymic nude
mice (Methods, "Animals"). Ten untreated mice received 0.5, 3 or 10 mg Fe/kg;
one 10 mg Fe/kg mouse was excluded for a high `Ka`, leaving 3 per dose group
(Figure 4). Four mice were pretreated with clodronate liposomes (clodrosome,
50 mg/kg IV once daily for 2 days) to deplete macrophages, and four with blank
phosphatidylcholine liposomes (376 mg/kg IV, 1.5 h before) to saturate RES
uptake; both groups then received 10 mg Fe/kg. Body weights are not reported.
The model's `population` metadata records the same facts.

# Source trace

| Element | Value in the model | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Blood mass balance | `d/dt(central) = -kel*central - k_central_liver*central + k_liver_central*liver` | Equation 1 (image e001), written on `Cp*Vp` |
| Liver mass balance | `d/dt(liver) = k_central_liver*central - k_liver_central*liver` | Equation 2 (image e002), written on `CL*VL` |
| Input `Ka*Dose` | IV bolus into `central`, `Ka` = 1 | Methods "Pharmacokinetic Modeling": `Ka` "should be approximately 1 for the intravenous bolus injection"; per-animal values not reported |
| `Kin` 0.5 / 3 / 10 mg Fe/kg | 38.527 / 1750.480 / 378027.6 1/s | Table 3 |
| `Kin` clodrosome / liposome + 10 mg Fe/kg | 4750.368 / 1770.913 1/s | Table 3 |
| `Kout` 0.5 / 3 / 10 mg Fe/kg | 0.014 / 0.098 / 0.365 1/s | Table 3 |
| `Kout` clodrosome / liposome + 10 mg Fe/kg | 0.128 / 5.875 1/s | Table 3 |
| `Ke` 0.5 / 3 / 10 mg Fe/kg | 0.008 / 0.015 / 0.025 1/s | Table 3 |
| `Ke` clodrosome / liposome + 10 mg Fe/kg | 0.015 / 0.015 1/s | Table 3 |
| `VL` | 1e-3 L/kg, fixed | Methods "Pharmacokinetic Modeling" |
| `Vp` | 0.1 L/kg, fixed | Not printed. Read by the maintainers from Figure 1c: Cp just after 10 mg Fe/kg is about 100 mg/L |
| Units | time s, dose mg Fe/kg, concentration mg Fe/L | Methods "Data analysis" |

In the model file the 10 mg Fe/kg untreated group is the reference, and each
other group enters as a log-ratio effect written as `log(<group value> /
<10 mg Fe/kg value>)`, so every group's rate constant equals its Table 3 mean.

```{r group-check}
groups <- data.frame(
  group = c("0.5 mg Fe/kg", "3 mg Fe/kg", "10 mg Fe/kg",
            "Clodrosome + 10 mg Fe/kg", "Liposome + 10 mg Fe/kg"),
  DOSE_IRONOXIDENANOPARTICLE_MGKG = c(0.5, 3, 10, 10, 10),
  CONMED_CLODRONATE = c(0, 0, 0, 1, 0),
  CONMED_PHOSPHATIDYLCHOLINE = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 1),
  kin_tab = c(38.527, 1750.480, 378027.6, 4750.368, 1770.913),
  kout_tab = c(0.014, 0.098, 0.365, 0.128, 5.875),
  ke_tab = c(0.008, 0.015, 0.025, 0.015, 0.015)
)
groups$id <- seq_len(nrow(groups))

# One dose and one observation at t = 0 per group, to read back the
# rate constants the model computes for each covariate combination.
ev_check <- bind_rows(
  groups |> mutate(time = 0, amt = DOSE_IRONOXIDENANOPARTICLE_MGKG, evid = 1),
  groups |> mutate(time = 0, amt = 0, evid = 0)
) |>
  mutate(cmt = "central") |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

chk <- rxSolve(mod, ev_check, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  left_join(groups, by = "id")

stopifnot(
  all(abs(chk$k_central_liver / chk$kin_tab - 1) < 1e-10),
  all(abs(chk$k_liver_central / chk$kout_tab - 1) < 1e-10),
  all(abs(chk$kel / chk$ke_tab - 1) < 1e-10)
)
```

# Why the printed rate constants cannot reproduce Figure 1c

Divided by the volumes, the two equations are a linear system in `Cp` and
`CL` whose matrix has trace `-(Ke + Kin + Kout)` and determinant `Ke * Kout`.
`Vp` and `VL` cancel from both, so the two disposition rates depend on Table 3
alone, whatever the unreported blood volume is.

```{r eigen}
eig <- groups |>
  mutate(
    tr = ke_tab + kin_tab + kout_tab,
    det = ke_tab * kout_tab,
    lambda_fast = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 * det)) / 2,
    # Stable form of the small root.
    lambda_slow = 2 * det / (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 * det)),
    t_fast_s = 1 / lambda_fast,
    thalf_slow_h = log(2) / lambda_slow / 3600,
    # Steady liver:blood concentration ratio during the slow phase, with the
    # paper's VL and the maintainers' Vp.
    ratio_liver_blood = kin_tab * 0.1 / ((kout_tab - lambda_slow) * 1e-3)
  )

eig |>
  select(group, t_fast_s, thalf_slow_h, ratio_liver_blood) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Group" = group,
    "Fast time constant (s)" = t_fast_s,
    "Slow half-life (h)" = thalf_slow_h,
    "Liver:blood concentration ratio" = ratio_liver_blood
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 6, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

With the printed values, blood and liver come to equilibrium within a
fraction of a second in every group, and then decline together with a
half-life of hours to about a year. Figure 1c (one untreated mouse at
10 mg Fe/kg, the paper's only fitted-curve figure) instead shows blood falling
from about 65 to about 6 mg/L over 1300 s (a half-life of about 5 min) while
the liver concentration **rises** steadily to about 11 mg/L, below the blood
concentration for most of the scan. That shape needs blood-to-liver exchange on
a time scale of minutes, which no blood volume can give with these rate
constants. Expressing the rates in other time units does not help either,
because the fast-to-slow ratio and the liver:blood ratio do not depend on the
time unit.

`Ke` alone does not reproduce the figure either: `log(2) / 0.025` is 28 s,
about ten times shorter than the blood decline in Figure 1c.

```{r eigen-check}
stopifnot(
  # Every group equilibrates within 0.1 s ...
  all(eig$t_fast_s < 0.1),
  # ... and then declines with a half-life above 3 h, against about 5 min in
  # Figure 1c.
  all(eig$thalf_slow_h > 3)
)
```

# Simulation and comparison with Figure 1c

Typical-value solve of each group over the 0-1300 s imaging window. The model
has no between-animal variability, so one subject per group is the whole
prediction.

```{r simulate}
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(0, 10^seq(-6, log10(1300), length.out = 200))))

ev_sim <- bind_rows(
  groups |> mutate(time = 0, amt = DOSE_IRONOXIDENANOPARTICLE_MGKG, evid = 1),
  tidyr::crossing(groups, time = obs_times) |> mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0)
) |>
  mutate(cmt = "central") |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

sim <- rxSolve(mod, ev_sim, returnType = "data.frame", atol = 1e-14,
               rtol = 1e-10) |>
  left_join(groups |> select(id, group), by = "id")
```

The Figure 1c points below are the maintainers' approximate reading by eye of
the paper's fitted (solid) curves, not of the noisy observations, and are good
to roughly 10-20%. The mismatch shown is several orders of magnitude.

```{r figure-1c, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5}
fig1c <- data.frame(
  time = c(20, 50, 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800, 900, 1000, 1100,
           1200, 1300),
  Cc = c(72, 63, 58, 50, 43, 37, 31, 26, 21, 17, 14, 11, 9, 7, 6),
  Cliver = c(1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 8.5, 9.5, 10, 10.5, 10.5, 11, 11, 11)
)

sim10 <- sim |>
  filter(group == "10 mg Fe/kg", time >= 1)

plot_df <- bind_rows(
  sim10 |> transmute(time, conc = Cc, tissue = "Blood", source = "Model (Table 3)"),
  sim10 |> transmute(time, conc = Cliver, tissue = "Liver", source = "Model (Table 3)"),
  fig1c |> transmute(time, conc = Cc, tissue = "Blood", source = "Figure 1c fit (read by eye)"),
  fig1c |> transmute(time, conc = Cliver, tissue = "Liver", source = "Figure 1c fit (read by eye)")
)

ggplot(plot_df, aes(time, conc, colour = tissue, linetype = source)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = filter(plot_df, source != "Model (Table 3)"), size = 1) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (s)", y = "SPIO concentration (mg Fe/L)",
       colour = NULL, linetype = NULL,
       title = "10 mg Fe/kg, untreated mouse",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 1c of Liu 2014 (and shows that it cannot).") +
  theme_bw()
```

The assertion below pins the failure, so that the mismatch is visible if
anything about the model changes. If a later correction or the authors'
model files make the model reproduce Figure 1c, this check fails and the
model needs to be updated.

```{r non-reproduction}
at_fig <- data.frame(
  time = fig1c$time,
  Cc_model = approx(sim10$time, sim10$Cc, xout = fig1c$time)$y,
  Cliver_model = approx(sim10$time, sim10$Cliver, xout = fig1c$time)$y
) |>
  left_join(fig1c, by = "time") |>
  mutate(blood_ratio = Cc_model / Cc, liver_ratio = Cliver_model / Cliver)

knitr::kable(
  at_fig |>
    select(time, Cc, Cc_model, Cliver, Cliver_model) |>
    dplyr::rename(
      "Time (s)" = time,
      "Blood, Figure 1c" = Cc,
      "Blood, model" = Cc_model,
      "Liver, Figure 1c" = Cliver,
      "Liver, model" = Cliver_model
    ),
  digits = 5
)

stopifnot(
  # Model blood concentration is more than 1000-fold below the published fit
  # at every time read from Figure 1c ...
  all(at_fig$blood_ratio < 1e-3),
  # ... and model liver concentration more than 100-fold above it.
  all(at_fig$liver_ratio > 100)
)
```

# Group profiles

```{r groups-plot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5}
sim |>
  filter(time >= 1e-6) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(Cc, Cliver), names_to = "output", values_to = "conc") |>
  mutate(output = ifelse(output == "Cc", "Blood", "Liver")) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, conc, colour = group)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~output) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (s)", y = "SPIO concentration (mg Fe/L)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# PKNCA validation

The paper reports no NCA. PKNCA is used here as a mass-balance check of the
solve: elimination is from blood only, so the blood AUC from zero to infinity
must equal `Dose / (Ke * Vp)`, and the terminal half-life must equal the slow
half-life computed above. The grid runs out to ten slow half-lives of each
group, because the slow phase carries almost all of the blood AUC.

```{r pknca}
nca_ev <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(groups)), function(i) {
  g <- groups[i, ]
  t_end <- 10 * eig$thalf_slow_h[i] * 3600
  tt <- sort(unique(c(0, 10^seq(-9, log10(t_end), length.out = 600))))
  bind_rows(
    g |> mutate(time = 0, amt = DOSE_IRONOXIDENANOPARTICLE_MGKG, evid = 1),
    g[rep(1, length(tt)), ] |> mutate(time = tt, amt = 0, evid = 0)
  )
})) |>
  mutate(cmt = "central") |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

nca_sim <- rxSolve(mod, nca_ev, returnType = "data.frame", atol = 1e-16,
                   rtol = 1e-11) |>
  left_join(groups |> select(id, group, DOSE_IRONOXIDENANOPARTICLE_MGKG), by = "id")

conc_obj <- PKNCAconc(
  nca_sim |> filter(!is.na(Cc)) |> select(id, group, time, Cc),
  Cc ~ time | group + id
)
dose_obj <- PKNCAdose(
  groups |> transmute(id, group, time = 0, dose = DOSE_IRONOXIDENANOPARTICLE_MGKG),
  dose ~ time | group + id,
  route = "intravascular"
)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
nca_res <- as.data.frame(pk.nca(PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals)))

nca_cmp <- nca_res |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("aucinf.obs", "half.life")) |>
  select(group, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  left_join(groups |> select(group, DOSE_IRONOXIDENANOPARTICLE_MGKG, ke_tab), by = "group") |>
  left_join(eig |> select(group, thalf_slow_h), by = "group") |>
  mutate(
    auc_expected = DOSE_IRONOXIDENANOPARTICLE_MGKG / (ke_tab * 0.1),
    thalf_expected = thalf_slow_h * 3600
  )

nca_cmp |>
  select(group, aucinf.obs, auc_expected, half.life, thalf_expected) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Group" = group,
    "Blood AUC0-inf, PKNCA (mg*s/L)" = aucinf.obs,
    "Dose / (Ke * Vp) (mg*s/L)" = auc_expected,
    "Terminal t1/2, PKNCA (s)" = half.life,
    "Slow t1/2, closed form (s)" = thalf_expected
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))

stopifnot(
  all(abs(nca_cmp$aucinf.obs / nca_cmp$auc_expected - 1) < 0.02),
  all(abs(nca_cmp$half.life / nca_cmp$thalf_expected - 1) < 0.02)
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **The printed rate constants do not reproduce the paper's fitted curve.**
  The maintainers packaged Table 3 exactly as printed and kept the mismatch
  visible above, rather than adjusting any value. The failure does not depend
  on the unreported blood volume or on the time unit. Table 3 is printed
  identically in Figure 4. The 10,000-fold change in `Kin` between 0.5 and
  10 mg Fe/kg is a further sign that the printed `Kin` is not the rate
  constant the fitted curves used. The units or scaling of `Kin`, and the
  values of `Vp` and `Ka`, are open questions for the authors.
- **`Vp` is not reported.** The paper names the blood distribution volume
  `Vp` but prints no value. The model fixes it at 0.1 L/kg, the maintainers'
  reading of Figure 1c (about 100 mg/L just after 10 mg Fe/kg). Mouse blood
  volume is about 0.07-0.08 L/kg, so the value is plausible, but it changes
  only the concentration scale and none of the conclusions above.
- **`Ka` is not reported and is taken as 1.** The equations scale the dose by
  `Ka`, which the Methods describe as the relation between injected dose and
  dose in blood, "approximately 1 for the intravenous bolus injection", and
  which was fitted per animal (one animal was excluded for a high `Ka`). Figure
  1b labels `Ka` in 1/s, but in the equations it multiplies a bolus dose, so the
  model reads it as an input fraction and enters the bolus unscaled.
- **The roughly 25 s manual injection is a bolus**, as in the paper.
- **No between-animal variability or residual error.** Each animal was fitted
  separately by least squares, and Table 3 gives the group mean +/- SD of
  3-4 per-animal estimates. Those SDs are not a population variance and are not
  encoded. The fit's sum of squared residuals (0.27 +/- 0.03) has no stated
  scale or weighting and gives no usable residual-error model, so the model is
  deterministic.
- **Dose level and pretreatment are categorical.** The paper gives one set of
  rate constants per group, not a function of dose. `DOSE_IRONOXIDENANOPARTICLE_MGKG`
  selects the 0.5 or 3 mg Fe/kg set, and any other value takes the 10 mg Fe/kg
  set. `CONMED_CLODRONATE` and `CONMED_PHOSPHATIDYLCHOLINE` select the two
  pretreatment sets, which were measured at 10 mg Fe/kg, and override the dose
  level.
- **Concentrations are MRI-derived.** The observed quantity is
  `Delta R2* / r2*` from vena cava and liver regions of interest, with r2*
  = 320 1/(mM*s) for free particles and about 350 for particles inside cells;
  the paper does not show how millimolar iron was converted to mg/L.
- **Sources checked.** The six supplementary files are image renderings of
  Tables 1-3 and contain no model code. The only correction notice (2015,
  PMC4370671) changes the Funding section only; checked on 2026-11-25.
